data.text: Review follow-up (2026-11-26). An external review of the uncommitted change (Codex, gpt-6.2-astra, medium reasoning) raised three P2 findings, all accepted and fixed. (1) runlimit-postgres/src/attempts/row.rs clamped stored instants before 1970 to the epoch, which moved an expired pre-epoch lease's backoff start and could disagree with the previous signed evaluator on a hand-edited row; instants now map exactly by shifting the epoch to the earliest BIGINT, so order and differences are preserved, the clamp is gone and the 'invalid attempt clock' refusal no longer exists. This supersedes the clamp decision and that detail string in the earlier comment. (2) AttemptLease's derived Debug printed the lease token; it is now a manual impl that omits it, with a doctest. (3) The backend obligations and example were on a private module and so absent from rustdoc; they are now on AttemptState, and 'storing the settled state is optional' is qualified to nondecreasing evaluation instants. Bound the single check and validated batch to the shard guards acquired for them. The first independent re-review found the analogous fixed-window capacity-denial regression. Fixed-window batches now do bounded cleanup for the full topology and check quota and capacity together in caller order. Fallible GCRA evaluation still precedes every clock/prune mutation and preserves suffix error precedence. A counted fixed-window algorithm test covers both exits. Final release probe on macOS arm64, 4,096 keys, one full shard, 901 samples from the in-lock clock sample to return: median 125 ns for quota denial and 167 ns for capacity denial at index zero. Focused all-feature package tests passed (84 including doctests), as did focused Clippy. Full final-tree verification and re-review in progress.

data.reason: Resolved the original four findings and all three follow-up findings. Single and batch sessions retain their inputs and routing. Fixed-window batches stop at either quota or capacity denial after bounded cleanup. GCRA arithmetic still precedes cleanup and later overflow wins. The changelog scopes allocation evidence to the measured paths. Both algorithms now describe entry writes, and only consuming commit methods on preflighted owners can apply them. Batch denial dispatch is exhaustive. In an isolated source copy, rustc rejected a premature write (E0603) and check/topology substitution (two E0061 diagnostics). The third independent uncommitted-tree review returned no findings. Final bash scripts/verify.sh passed on macOS arm64 with pinned Rust 1.100.0, including all four Clippy configurations, all six matrix parts, rustdoc and all HTTP smoke profiles. Three Runledger phased-handler deadline assertions failed on the initial run, passed in isolation and passed in the final full run. The final release probe reproduced medians of 125 ns for quota denial and 167 ns for capacity denial across 901 samples each, timed from the in-lock clock to return for 4096 keys on one shard.

data.text: PR #129 fixed-window stress test on macOS arm64, Rust 1.100.0, used clean master 445a8aaa and head 055d8d55. Out-of-tree two-pass prototype requires the shared fail-closed remaining_quota arithmetic and lazy pending-insertion counts. The initial prototype panicked and partially charged an injected over-limit batch. With the corrections, 384,000 deterministic operations matched decisions and observer traces, 76,800 competing calls preserved exact accounting, and debug/release runlimit-memory suites passed. Eight contenders on 4,096 warmed keys achieved 8,618/4,854/9,468 batches per second for master/PR/corrected. All-allowed p99 was 1.78/3.28/2.04 ms. The corrected late-denial path allocated zero after the clock sample versus 576 KiB on the PR. Large synchronized expiry was still modestly slower than master. This is prototype evidence; the performance fix has not landed.

fields.title: Remove buffered fixed-window batch writes while retaining atomic quota and capacity preflight

data.text: Implementation pushed as 88edfc5c to PR #129. Fixed-window preflight checks each occupied or vacant key in input order, uses fail-closed quota arithmetic, and lazily counts projected insertions. A private preflighted owner retains the original locks and checks into commit. The map entry API lets commit reuse a vacant or expired slot. Release Runlimit tests pass, including denial with a corrupt late counter and no prefix charge. Seven compile diagnostics confirm premature commit, proof forgery, check substitution and four foreign configuration calls are rejected. Production trace probes match master across 384,000 fixed-window operations and a further 30,000 operations per algorithm. One hundred 8-thread rounds (76,800 calls) found exact accounting. Local full verification, hosted checks and PR-wide review in progress.

Final PR #129 head aa3e3ef0 passed complete pinned Rust 1.100.0 verification on macOS arm64 with two Rust test threads and in hosted Linux CI (https://github.com/bpcakes/batter/actions/runs/45861638570). Hosted native Runlimit PostgreSQL, macOS subprocess, verified-tree and repository policy checks passed. The clean full-PR code review followed a repair that narrowed single-check outcomes to enforced or shadow denials and GCRA arithmetic failures to quota-only denials. Nine negative compile probes passed. Release crate tests passed, 384,000 fixed-window operations and 30,000 per-backend trace operations matched master, and 76,800 contending calls reconciled exactly. A warmed 4,096-key late denial allocated 0 bytes under lock compared with 576 KiB on the previous PR. Median one-shard warmed allowed lock time was 54.8 microseconds versus 70.1 on master and 123.3 on the previous PR. Eight-caller warmed p99 was 3.29 ms versus 3.91 ms on master. Synthetic same-process measurements against master showed about 1% longer whole calls for 16-shard cold insertion and simultaneous expiry, around 7 ns extra per warmed single check and about 5% on warmed 32- and 4,096-key GCRA batches. The PR description includes the measurements and verification links. GitHub reports the PR mergeable with zero review threads.

data.reason: Removed the fixed-window per-key write buffer, preserved fail-closed and atomic accounting, and verified merge-ready PR #129 at aa3e3ef0 on macOS and hosted Linux.

fields.description:
## Finding
runlimit-postgres carries three copies of the limiter shell (pool, config, observer, Debug, migrate, guarded bounded connection) in src/lib.rs, src/gcra.rs and src/attempts.rs, and they have drifted: PostgresAttemptLimiter::migrate clones ATTEMPTS_MIGRATOR.migrations and always retires its connection while the other two re-invoke sqlx::migrate! and reuse it on success; PostgresLimiter's Debug uses finish_non_exhaustive, PostgresGcraLimiter's finish, and PostgresAttemptLimiter has neither Debug nor config(). CheckTransaction refreshes SET LOCAL timeouts before every statement and commit, while maintenance.rs exposes raw helpers that gcra::cleanup_transaction must pair by hand three times. The authoritative-elapsed subtraction exists in admission.rs and gcra/response.rs. tests/postgres.rs, tests/gcra.rs and tests/attempts.rs each reimplement the disposable-schema harness and the XOR shard-key helper.

## Remediation
One private limiter base owning pool, config, observer, Debug, migration and bounded guarded connections; one bounded transaction generic over the check and maintenance families that refreshes timeouts itself; one pending-response finisher; one shared live-test schema fixture.

## Public surface
Additive only: PostgresAttemptLimiter gains Debug and config(), and new becomes const. No hard cut. Behaviour notes belong in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md.

Related: batter-ctk7.12 (connection disposition classifier) builds on the single transaction and guard this leaves behind.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The three limiters share one private base for pool, config, observer, Debug, migrate and bounded connection acquisition; one transaction type refreshes server timeouts before every statement and commit for checks and cleanup; one function subtracts authoritative elapsed time for both quota limiters; the three live suites use one schema fixture; scripts/verify.sh and the live runlimit-postgres suites pass.
fields.title: Share one PostgreSQL limiter shell, bounded transaction, pending-response finisher and live-test schema fixture in runlimit-postgres

data.text: Implemented on worktree/calm-harbor-06e1 (uncommitted, base aa3e3ef0). Claims confirmed against the code before the change: (1) three migrate bodies, two re-invoking sqlx::migrate! with reuse-on-success and the attempt one cloning ATTEMPTS_MIGRATOR.migrations and always closing; (2) CheckTransaction refreshed timeouts itself while gcra::cleanup_transaction paired set_maintenance_server_timeouts by hand three times; (3) acquisition+guard+deadline, observer emission and elapsed-time subtraction duplicated, Debug finish vs finish_non_exhaustive, PostgresAttemptLimiter without Debug or config(); (4) three schema harnesses and two XOR shard-key helpers in tests. Change: src/base.rs (PgLimiterBase<O>: pool, config, observer, Debug, migrate, bounded connections, quota observation), src/transaction.rs (ConnectionOutcome, guard with an explicit OnDrop state instead of armed: bool and reuse(), BoundedConnection<F>, BoundedTransaction<F> over the Check and Maintenance families), src/pending.rs (Pending<A>::finish is the only elapsed-time subtraction; gcra/response.rs removed, its tests moved), admission::finalize shared by both quota limiters, tests/support/mod.rs (IsolatedSchema, shard-key helpers) used by postgres.rs, gcra.rs, attempts.rs and the new tests/migrate.rs. File budget: admission.rs (588) and tests/attempts.rs (780) leave the exemption list; lib.rs ceiling 1252->1083, tests/postgres.rs 2841->2704. Behaviour notes are in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md: attempt migrate reuses its session after success; GCRA Debug ends with '..'; cleanup commit refreshes timeouts before the budget check, which changes the phase reported when the deadline has already passed at commit (no deterministic test for that race). Relation to batter-ctk7.12: reuse(&mut self) and the direct inner.rollback() path are gone and every path now passes one guard and one transaction type, but the single error-origin classifier and commit(decision)/deny(decision) finalizers it asks for are not done here.

Baseline before the change on the same database: attempts 18, gcra 23, postgres 32 passed. New tests: tests/migrate.rs every_migration_returns_its_session_only_after_success (all three limiters; success reuses the session, a checksum failure retires it), transaction.rs unit tests for pre-commit classification in both families, base.rs every_limiter_exposes_the_same_shell, pending.rs elapsed-time and storage-capacity tests. Limitations: hosted CI not run; Linux not run locally; the cleanup-commit deadline race described in the CHANGELOG has no deterministic test; no public-API surface diff tool was run (the public changes are additive: Debug, config() and const new on PostgresAttemptLimiter). Not committed: awaiting an explicit request.

Rounds 1-4 raised nine findings, each verified against the code, confirmed and fixed; round 5 raised none; none was pre-existing, so nothing was logged for later. Round 1: the migration live test proved session reuse but not unlock (advisory locks are reentrant), now also asserts via pg_locks from another session that the returned session holds no advisory lock; Pending::finish borrowed instead of consuming the evaluated allowances, costing an allocation per allowed fixed-window check; the changelog misdescribed the cleanup commit deadline cases. Round 4: the commit-deadline unit test runs on a paused Tokio clock (tokio test-util added to dev-dependencies, Cargo.lock unchanged); the changelog describes the deadline cases by what the client observes. fields.description:
## Finding (pre-existing; raised by Codex review of PR #130, not introduced there)
In runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/transaction.rs, BoundedTransaction::execute, fetch_all and fetch_one refresh the server timeouts and then pass the statement to before_commit, which wraps it in timeout_at(deadline, ..). The remaining budget is checked when the refresh is computed (protocol::remaining_server_timeout_settings) but not again after the refresh returns. If the refresh starts within budget and its response arrives at or after the deadline, the statement is still polled: Tokio polls the wrapped future before the timer, so the SQL is sent, the client timer then fires, and an otherwise reusable connection is retired (ConnectionOutcome::MustClose) for a statement that could only time out. Only the commit path re-checks (attempt_commit).

The same sequence existed before the shared transaction: CheckTransaction::prepare followed by check_before_commit in admission.rs, and set_maintenance_server_timeouts followed by maintenance_before_commit in maintenance.rs and gcra.rs (base aa3e3ef0).

## Proposed remediation
Check the deadline at entry to before_commit and return a reusable pre-commit timeout without polling the step, covered by a poll-recording future as attempt_commit is. This is a runtime break under the repository rule: a statement that today finishes inside the client timer's slack, and with it a denial the check would have returned, becomes TimedOutBeforeCommit. It needs a Breaking CHANGELOG entry with before/after handling and log text for check, check_all, admit and cleanup.

## Related
batter-2oht (shared transaction), batter-ctk7.12 (single connection-disposition classifier).
fields.acceptance_criteria: No pre-commit statement is polled once the operation deadline has been reached, proven by a poll-recording unit test for both families; the connection stays reusable in that case; the runtime break is recorded in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after handling and log text; live runlimit-postgres suites pass.
fields.title: runlimit-postgres sends a pre-commit statement after its timeout refresh used up the operation deadline

data.text: Correction to the description: the statement that follows an over-budget refresh is not certain to time out. Tokio polls the statement before the timer, so a ready database result can win and the call can still return (for example a denial on the last preflight). The connection is retired only when the client timer fires first.
